READING

**The environmental baseline**
The strongroom runs at 62 % RH with an 11-point seasonal swing against a standard of 45–55 % and a swing under 5. The gap is not marginal: the absolute level is 7–17 points above the upper tolerance and the swing is more than double what is acceptable. For iron gall ink—hygroscopic, acidic and mechanically fragile—and for acidic board, this is an active threat. The 2019–2025 resurvey confirms the damage is accelerating: 370 items moved into the unusable band in six years, roughly 62 per year. The environment is the mechanism producing the losses; it is not a background condition.

**What buffered enclosures actually do**
LINDCASTER relies in part on the claim that buffered enclosures hold an item's microclimate within 3 points of its packing condition for eight to twelve years. This is true, but the packing condition in this strongroom is approximately 62 % RH. An enclosure holding within 3 points of 62 % holds the item at 59–65 % RH—still far outside the 45–55 % standard. Buffered enclosures damp the rate of environmental swing; they do not substitute for a controlled environment. They would meaningfully protect items only if the baseline were already close to standard. Here it is not. The enclosures are not a proxy for the plant.

**The conservator's written report**
Idris Sankey-Marchmont has stated in writing that rehousing and aqueous treatment carried out into the strongroom as it stands will need to be repeated within a decade. This is a professional finding, not a precautionary caveat. Its implications for LINDCASTER are severe: the entire GBP 340,000 conservation spend is not a permanent investment but a time-limited holding measure. Around 2036–2038 the Institute would face the same outlay again, in an environment still outside standard, without any guarantee of equivalent funding. HAVERSHOLT's conservation spend of GBP 45,000, made into a corrected environment, carries no equivalent repeat-cost liability. The conservator's report effectively changes the accounting for LINDCASTER: its 1,360-item figure is not a net achievement but a gross one that depreciates within a decade.

**The plant quote and ordering deadline**
The Threlkeld Environmental quote of GBP 295,000 is held to 2027-01-30. Commissioning is set for 2027-05-29. The 14-week lead time means the order must be placed by approximately 20 February 2027; ordering by 30 January satisfies both the price-hold deadline and the lead-time requirement simultaneously. Today is 2026-08-25, leaving roughly five months to act. That is adequate but not open-ended. If LINDCASTER is chosen and no order is placed, the current quote lapses. Any future plant procurement—including one funded by the 2029-30 programme—would be at an unquoted, likely higher price in a different market. LINDCASTER thus risks compounding the environmental problem with an increased future plant cost.

**The 2029-30 capital programme**
The unallocated GBP 400,000 line is the foundation of LINDCASTER's plant strategy. The board sets allocations in November 2028; nothing is committed. Capital lines can be redirected between now and that meeting. This risk runs both ways, however: HAVERSHOLT also relies on the 2029-30 programme for the bulk of its conservation. The critical difference is what the programme buys in each scenario. Under LINDCASTER, it buys a plant at an unquoted price to correct an environment that is damaging items already treated—and those treatments, per the conservator, will need repeating before the plant even operates. Under HAVERSHOLT, the environment is already corrected by mid-2027; the 2029-30 programme buys conservation in a stable environment at GBP 250 per item, producing up to 1,600 permanently treated items. That is more items than LINDCASTER treats now, and those treatments are permanent.

**Item numbers and what they mean**
LINDCASTER treats 1,360 items against HAVERSHOLT's 180. This is the most compelling argument for LINDCASTER and should be taken seriously. But the figure must be read against the conservator's finding. The 1,360 number is not a permanent outcome; it is a rolling commitment to repeat expenditure in a continuing bad environment. The 2,840 items on iron gall ink or acidic board that LINDCASTER does not reach continue to deteriorate at or above the current rate. HAVERSHOLT, by fixing the environment for all 4,200 items from mid-2027, stops the deterioration clock universally: no further items move into the unusable band after commissioning, and every conservation pound spent thereafter—from the 2029-30 programme or any subsequent source—is a permanent rather than a depreciating gain.

**The unusable band**
1,010 items are currently unusable. LINDCASTER could reach all 1,010 and 350 more; HAVERSHOLT reaches 180 total. The question is what treatment in each environment achieves. In a continuing 62 % environment, conservation on unusable items may restore some handleability, but the conditions that produced the damage remain unchanged and the conservator's written view is that the work will need redoing. Under HAVERSHOLT, the 1,010 items are not treated now but are stabilised at their present state in a controlled environment from May 2027; future conservation—including from the 2029-30 programme—makes any treatment of them permanent. Neither course resolves the unusable band immediately and completely, but HAVERSHOLT resolves the mechanism creating it.

**Spending the bequest within the deadline**
Both courses can meet the 2028-09-30 deadline without difficulty. Under HAVERSHOLT, the plant order is placed by January 2027, commissioning completes May 2027, and the residual GBP 45,000 of conservation represents roughly 2.5 months of contract work, completable well before September 2028. Under LINDCASTER, 1,360 items at 70 per month takes approximately 19–20 months; ordered in September 2026 and started by November 2026, work completes around June 2028. Neither course presents a deadline problem.

**The decisive comparison**
HAVERSHOLT: GBP 295,000 permanently corrects the environment for all 4,200 items from mid-2027 onward. GBP 45,000 treats 180 items permanently. If the 2029-30 programme is secured, up to 1,600 further items are treated permanently in a controlled environment. Total permanent conservation, programme included: approximately 1,780 items.

LINDCASTER: GBP 340,000 treats 1,360 items in a continuing bad environment. Per the conservator's written report, those treatments are not permanent; they require repetition within a decade. The 2,840 remaining at-risk items continue deteriorating indefinitely. The 2029-30 programme is needed to buy the plant, at an unquoted price, to begin correcting an environment that has been damaging the collection—and re-damaging already-treated items—throughout the interval. The 1,360 figure is not additive to what follows; much of it is consumed by the repetition requirement.

The bequest is a one-time resource. The question is whether to use it to change the structural conditions under which everything else happens, or to spend it on individual treatments that the Institute's own conservator has certified will not last. HAVERSHOLT answers that question clearly.

---

READING
The plant quote expires 2027-01-30 and the conservator has certified in writing that every conservation pound spent in the current environment depreciates within a decade; HAVERSHOLT corrects the root cause for all 4,200 items within the bequest ceiling and within the quote deadline, making every subsequent treatment permanent, while LINDCASTER spends the full bequest on impermanent work and leaves the structural cause unaddressed. The 2029-30 programme is better applied to scalable, permanent conservation after the environment is fixed than to an unquoted plant replacement after treated items have begun re-deteriorating.

CALL
HAVERSHOLT

GROUNDS
The conservator's written finding that treatment in the current environment must be repeated within a decade renders LINDCASTER's entire spend impermanent, and HAVERSHOLT—correcting the root cause for all 4,200 items within the bequest ceiling and before the quote lapses—is the only course that converts every subsequent conservation pound into a lasting result.
